title: Early-sampler rubric + hunchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a tiny, targeted sanity check on recent output deltas after the small-kv-cache change (PR 572). Not intended to be exhaustive — just a fast loop to validate obvious regressions and capture prompts/examples to escalate if needed.

Notes / context:
- Observed a subtle drift in paraphrase fidelity on short prompts (<= 32 tokens) after cache refactor. Hypothesis: new cache eviction interacts with continuous-batching and causes slightly older KV state to be reused for very short sequences when batching is tight.
- Test surface: hosted-api, model family: open-lms/ll-14b-qa-v1 (quantized variant), route: /v1/generate (default batching window).
- Trigger ticket: RINF-2043 (linked). SRE noted increased 5xx during peak burst windows, but the perf graphs looked fine — this doc targets correctness signal only.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (0-3, keep it intentionally coarse):
0 = catastrophic (wrong class, unsafe, hallucinating major facts)
1 = incorrect/low-quality (misses required detail, logically inconsistent)
2 = acceptable with deficits (minor omissions, slight phrasing issues, still usable)
3 = good (accurate, concise, preserves intent)

Sampling plan:
- N = 40 short prompts sampled from product telemetry (random seed 23) + 10 contrived edge prompts (context boundary, repeated tokens).
- Run baseline (pre-PR-572) and post-change. Compare token-level diffs, BLEU-ish-ish, and rubric score assignments.
- Manual triage for any item where score drops by >=1 or output length changes >25% for same semantic content.

Representative prompts + outputs (manually annotated):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the refund policy for physical goods." (len 9)
   Baseline: "If a physical item arrives damaged, customers can return within 30 days for a full refund; shipping costs are refunded if the damage was seller-caused."
   Post-change: "Customers can return damaged items within 30 days. Shipping may be refunded."
   Delta notes: shorter, lost conditional about seller-caused shipping refund. Score baseline=3, post=2.

2) Prompt: "How do I reset my API key?" (len 6)
   Baseline: "Go to Settings → API keys → Revoke then Create new. Update your app with the new key."
   Post-change: "Open Settings, revoke the key, then create a new one."
   Delta: essentially the same; micro-phrasing. Score both=3.

3) Prompt: "List the steps to onboard a new account with SSO and SCIM." (len 12)
   Baseline: multi-step, includes SCIM provisioning note + permission mapping
   Post-change: missing the permission mapping bullet, reused earlier sentence structure from previous sample (possible caching artifact). Score baseline=3, post=1. Actionable: escalate if reproducible.

4) Prompt: "Does the platform store customer prompts?" (len 7)
   Baseline: "We store prompt text for X days for debugging; opt-out available via enterprise settings."
   Post-change: hallucinated retention period: "We store prompt text for 90 days..." (we don't use absolute numbers) Score baseline=3, post=0 (safety/policy hallucination). High priority.

Quick summary of findings so far:
- Overall drop in mean rubric score across the 50-sample set: baseline mean=2.68, post-change mean=2.34.
- High-severity hallucination (example 4) seen twice in the post-change set -> file a P0 regression.
- Many small compressions/truncations on very short inputs (<=10 tokens), indicating KV re-use or truncation logic issue.
- No obvious throughput/latency signal correlated in the short sniff; this looks correctness-first.

Immediate next steps (prioritized):
1) Re-run failing samples with cache disabled at runtime flag (cache=false) to confirm cache as causal. Quick A/B in staging; add results to RINF-2043.
2) Add golden prompt set (this doc's 50 prompts) to the micro-regression pipeline with automated rubric baseline scoring. Keep this set under product/qa review for 2 weeks.
3) For hallucination example, extract full model trace (KV states + input ids) and attach to ticket. Ask infra to preserve the runtime logs for the failing time window (Slack tag @infra).
4) If reproduces deterministically, revert the specific cache-eviction change or add a guard (skip reuse when seq_len <= 16) as temporary mitigant.

Open questions / hunches:
- Could continuous-batching heuristics be folding unrelated requests into the same batch and copying KV pointers incorrectly? Need code review of fence/ownership in PR 572.
- Does the quantization variant exacerbate this (observed in two different quantized builds)? Compare fp16 baseline.
- Are short prompts more affected because shared KV entries have less distinguishing context?

Scratch TODOs (for me):
- [ ] Run 200-sample bootstrap (ran 50) and compute confidence intervals on mean delta.
- [ ] Ask Sasha to re-run with fp16 model and attach token-diff heatmap.
- [ ] Post a short note in #eng-serving with the two worst examples and link to ticket.
- [ ] Add these examples to a new folder in drive: shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/regressions/night-sweeps (if approved by PM).

Useful logs/commands I used:
- curl to hit hosted: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"open-lms/ll-14b-qa-v1","prompt":"..."}'
- local trace: docker logs rinf-runtime-01 | rg "kv-evict"

If this looks real/deterministic after the A/B, escalate to @SRE and @runtime-owners. Will iterate here and then prepare a short one-pager for product if there's customer-facing impact.

Mini-changelog:
- 2025-11-10: initial draft, collected 50-sample set, ran initial baseline vs post-change smoke.
- 2025-11-12: added rubric, sample annotations, and next steps.

Random notes to self: avoid rushing revert if it fixes correctness but regresses perf. Prioritize a targeted guard or patch for short-sequence reuse.
